dedupe_keys.name: nrc state of the art reactor consequence analyses soarca of severe accidents at surry and peach bottom

description: The State-of-the-Art Reactor Consequence Analyses (SOARCA) project, started by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in 2007, develops best estimates of the offsite radiological health consequences of potential severe reactor accidents. It analysed the Surry Power Station in Virginia and the Peach Bottom Atomic Power Station in Pennsylvania, combining up-to-date plant layout and operations information with local population data and emergency preparedness plans, and using state-of-the-art computer codes that incorporate decades of severe accident research. The process follows five steps: selecting accident scenarios, modelling onsite accident progression and mitigation, modelling offsite release, modelling emergency response, and modelling health effects. Public comments were taken on the draft NUREG-1935 and public meetings were held in February 2012, and the final report was published in November 2012 with peer review letters; technical support is in NUREG/CR-7110 volumes 1 and 2. Access: web page and reports, free; no licence is stated. Coverage is two U.S. plants and specific scenarios, so results cannot be transferred directly. It suits emergency response and consequence scenario design for nuclear siting and evacuation studies, and relates to the NRC datasets on US nuclear facilities catalogued here.

outcomes: Best-estimate offsite consequences of potential severe accidents at Surry and Peach Bottom: existing resources and procedures can stop, slow or reduce accidents, uncontrolled accidents take much longer and release much less radioactive material than earlier analyses suggested, and the analysed accidents would cause essentially zero immediate deaths and a very small increase in long-term cancer risk.
